content.title: Finding small Tisa salinity pockets within routine survey costs

facts.text: TloCare reports that its four-hectare sampling grid misses saline pockets of 0.3–0.8 hectares. Denser sampling adds fieldwork, laboratory costs and delivery time; the company says it cannot afford generally denser sampling.

gušće uzorkovanje znači više terena, više laboratorijskih troškova i duži rok isporuke
we can't afford to sample more densely.

facts.text: The company has GPS coordinates and laboratory results for about 18,000 points from ten years. Its stated customer outputs cover pH, phosphorus, potassium, humus and liming needs, and it uses SRPS sampling and analysis protocols; these statements do not establish historical ECe or ESP coverage.

facts.text: TloCare has two programmers and one GIS specialist able to allocate up to one-third of their time to development, with occasional field-team support. Its existing spatial database and portal use PostGIS and Leaflet.

facts.text: Kosanović’s sunflower-farm study used regression-kriging with both EM38 conductivity and pXRF sodium measurements. It reported lower cross-validation errors than ordinary kriging without those covariates.

sources.quote: Apparent electrical conductivity (ECa) from an EM38 survey and total sodium content from pXRF scanning served as covariates
RK achieved RMSE of 2.7 mS/m for ECe and 2.9 cmol/kg for ESP, compared with 3.8 and 4.2 for ordinary kriging without covariates.

facts.text: His sample-reduction study found unstable nugget estimates below 30 cores, compromising kriging weights. His flooded-field study distinguished stable conductivity zones from transitions with lower temporal stability.

sources.quote: Nugget variance estimates became unstable below n=30, compromising kriging weights.
Zones of lower stability were located on sloping transitions between microrelief elements.

inferences: This suggests a strong methodological fit, but published sunflower results do not validate detection of TloCare’s small Tisa pockets or an EM38-only workflow. Conductivity is a proxy: texture, moisture and survey timing could produce missed pockets or false positives.

Savings likely depend on balancing calibration density against advance sensor-survey costs and repeat visits. Historical records could help only after checking salinity coverage and protocol comparability; archive size alone does not establish usable reference labels.

This joint-project proposal is conditional: sustained researcher availability remains unconfirmed despite openness to this format. A bounded field pilot appears more practical than immediate portal development.
proposedActions: Propose a Tisa-field pilot comparing the four-hectare grid, EM38-assisted regression-kriging and EM38-plus-pXRF regression-kriging. TloCare would nominate fields and supply records; Kosanović would design calibration and sensing. Use separate tuning fields and densely laboratory-referenced held-out Tisa fields; verify spatial independence and freeze configuration selection before evaluation. Test local conductivity–salinity calibration rather than importing published spacing. Define reference pockets using an agreed laboratory salinity threshold. Proposed go/no-go for the best tuning-selected configuration: higher detection of confirmed 0.3–0.8-hectare pockets than the grid, with no greater false-positive area, routine cost per hectare or turnaround. Count a pocket as detected when predictions cover at least half its reference polygon; divide by all confirmed target-size pockets. Measure false-positive hectares over reference-confirmed non-saline hectares. Require uncertainty bounds supporting improvement; unresolved reference areas or insufficient pockets prevent a pass. Include advance sensing, consumables and repeat visits in recurring costs, while reporting independent validation costs separately.

Propose six to eight weeks after access and bookings are secured: audit archive targets, depths, dates and laboratory comparability; agree evaluation precision and fund reference sampling; then conduct fieldwork and analysis. Deliver zone and uncertainty layers before the soil-sampling crew’s dispatch. Explicitly schedule and cost any earlier sensor visit; if predictions must precede every field visit, treat advance-data availability as a prerequisite.

Keep implementation within the stated staffing allocation: initially export PostGIS-compatible layers for Leaflet review rather than build new portal functions. Propose repeat measurements across changing moisture conditions, especially transitions, before reusing surveys. Test affordable calibration densities without assuming sparse samples remain reliable; confirm instrument bookings, consumables funding and field support before starting.
questions: Can Kosanović confirm sustained joint-project availability, his proposed role and feasible instrument-booking terms?
Can TloCare secure representative Tisa fields, independent reference-sampling access and historical salinity records with depth, date and laboratory metadata?
What laboratory salinity threshold, detection improvement, false-positive tolerance, cost ceiling and turnaround limit should govern acceptance?

content.markdown:
# Finding small Tisa salinity pockets within routine survey costs

## Verified facts
- TloCare reports that its four-hectare sampling grid misses saline pockets of 0.3–0.8 hectares. Denser sampling adds fieldwork, laboratory costs and delivery time; the company says it cannot afford generally denser sampling. [F1]
- The company has GPS coordinates and laboratory results for about 18,000 points from ten years. Its stated customer outputs cover pH, phosphorus, potassium, humus and liming needs, and it uses SRPS sampling and analysis protocols; these statements do not establish historical ECe or ESP coverage. [F2]
- TloCare reports unsuccessful NDVI-guided adaptive sampling because salinity was not clearly visible in early-spring vegetation indices. [F3]
- Kosanović lists openness to company joint projects, availability for short consultancy visits and a preference for field-data collection. His instruments are available to external partners subject to scheduling and consumables cost recovery. [F4]
- TloCare has two programmers and one GIS specialist able to allocate up to one-third of their time to development, with occasional field-team support. Its existing spatial database and portal use PostGIS and Leaflet. [F5]
- Kosanović’s sunflower-farm study used regression-kriging with both EM38 conductivity and pXRF sodium measurements. It reported lower cross-validation errors than ordinary kriging without those covariates. [F6]
- His sample-reduction study found unstable nugget estimates below 30 cores, compromising kriging weights. His flooded-field study distinguished stable conductivity zones from transitions with lower temporal stability. [F7]

## Potential benefits
- For the company: The pilot could establish whether small salinity pockets can be located more reliably without increasing routine cost or turnaround, and identify when advance sensing is economical.
- For the researcher: Subject to agreement and access, the project could provide Tisa floodplain measurements for testing local calibration, sensor combinations and the sampling-density trade-off at small-pocket scale.

## Our inference
- This suggests a strong methodological fit, but published sunflower results do not validate detection of TloCare’s small Tisa pockets or an EM38-only workflow. Conductivity is a proxy: texture, moisture and survey timing could produce missed pockets or false positives.
- Savings likely depend on balancing calibration density against advance sensor-survey costs and repeat visits. Historical records could help only after checking salinity coverage and protocol comparability; archive size alone does not establish usable reference labels.
- This joint-project proposal is conditional: sustained researcher availability remains unconfirmed despite openness to this format. A bounded field pilot appears more practical than immediate portal development.

## Proposed next steps
- Propose a Tisa-field pilot comparing the four-hectare grid, EM38-assisted regression-kriging and EM38-plus-pXRF regression-kriging. TloCare would nominate fields and supply records; Kosanović would design calibration and sensing. Use separate tuning fields and densely laboratory-referenced held-out Tisa fields; verify spatial independence and freeze configuration selection before evaluation. Test local conductivity–salinity calibration rather than importing published spacing. Define reference pockets using an agreed laboratory salinity threshold. Proposed go/no-go for the best tuning-selected configuration: higher detection of confirmed 0.3–0.8-hectare pockets than the grid, with no greater false-positive area, routine cost per hectare or turnaround. Count a pocket as detected when predictions cover at least half its reference polygon; divide by all confirmed target-size pockets. Measure false-positive hectares over reference-confirmed non-saline hectares. Require uncertainty bounds supporting improvement; unresolved reference areas or insufficient pockets prevent a pass. Include advance sensing, consumables and repeat visits in recurring costs, while reporting independent validation costs separately.
- Propose six to eight weeks after access and bookings are secured: audit archive targets, depths, dates and laboratory comparability; agree evaluation precision and fund reference sampling; then conduct fieldwork and analysis. Deliver zone and uncertainty layers before the soil-sampling crew’s dispatch. Explicitly schedule and cost any earlier sensor visit; if predictions must precede every field visit, treat advance-data availability as a prerequisite.
- Keep implementation within the stated staffing allocation: initially export PostGIS-compatible layers for Leaflet review rather than build new portal functions. Propose repeat measurements across changing moisture conditions, especially transitions, before reusing surveys. Test affordable calibration densities without assuming sparse samples remain reliable; confirm instrument bookings, consumables funding and field support before starting.

## Open questions
- Can Kosanović confirm sustained joint-project availability, his proposed role and feasible instrument-booking terms?
- Can TloCare secure representative Tisa fields, independent reference-sampling access and historical salinity records with depth, date and laboratory metadata?
- What laboratory salinity threshold, detection improvement, false-positive tolerance, cost ceiling and turnaround limit should govern acceptance?
- Is a separately costed advance sensor visit acceptable before soil-sampling dispatch, and can the parties agree pilot funding, staff allocation and data-use terms?
